_meta.indication: Indicated in adults for prevention of PONV (alone or in combination with an antiemetic of a different class) and treatment of PONV in patients who have received antiemetic prophylaxis with an agent of a different class or have not received prophylaxis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center trial in patients undergoing general anesthesia and elective surgery
pivotal_trials.population: 342 patients undergoing general anesthesia and elective surgery; mean age 54 years, 65% female
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete Response, defined as absence of any episode of emesis or use of rescue medication within the first 24 hours postoperatively
pivotal_trials.result: Complete Response 44% (78/176) BARHEMSYS 5 mg vs 33% (54/166) placebo; difference 12% (95% CI 2%, 22%)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 2 (prevention of PONV, combination with another antiemetic)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center trial; BARHEMSYS given in combination with another non-dopaminergic antiemetic
pivotal_trials.population: 1,147 patients undergoing general anesthesia and elective surgery; mean age 49 years, 97% female
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete Response, defined as absence of any episode of emesis or use of rescue medication within the first 24 hours postoperatively
pivotal_trials.n: 1,147 (BARHEMSYS 5 mg with another antiemetic n=572, placebo with another antiemetic n=575)
pivotal_trials.result: Complete Response 58% (330/572) BARHEMSYS 5 mg with another antiemetic vs 47% (268/575) placebo; difference 11% (95% CI 5%, 17%)

key_safety: For prevention (BARHEMSYS 5 mg, N=748), common adverse reactions included chills (4%), hypokalemia (4%), procedural hypotension (3%), abdominal distension (2%); for treatment (10 mg, N=418) the most common was infusion site pain (6% vs placebo 4%). BARHEMSYS causes dose- and concentration-dependent QT prolongation.
target_moa: Selective dopamine-2 (D2) and dopamine-3 (D3) receptor antagonist; D2 receptors in the chemoreceptor trigger zone and D3 receptors in the area postrema play a role in emesis

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions

summary.text: Standard-review 505(b)(2) NDA for amisulpride injection for prevention and treatment of PONV, submitted October 5, 2017; the application received two Complete Response letters (10/05/2018 and 5/2/19) for manufacturing facility deficiencies, was resubmitted August 26, 2019, and was approved effective on the date of the approval letter (signed 02/26/2020), with no expedited-program designations and not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated October 5, 2017, received October 5, 2017, and your amendments, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Barhemsys (amisulpride) injection, for intravenous use.

The original NDA 209510 for amisulpride injection (APD421) was submitted on 10/05/2017. Due to the deficiencies in facility inspection, NDA 209510 amisulpride injection had received a complete response (CR) on 10/05/2018. The NDA received a 2nd CR on 5/2/19 in response to Applicant's 11/5/18 resubmission because the facility issues were not adequately addressed.
We acknowledge receipt of your amendment dated August 26, 2019, which constituted a complete response to our May 2, 2019, action letter.
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.

Your application for Barhemsys was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease.
